chunks: Hammad ibn Isa from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"When a man catches game while in the Sanctuary (Haram) and he is in the state of Ihram, it is obligatory for him to ransom it, and no one should eat it. And if he catches it in the open (Hill), the one who is not in Ihram may eat it, and the ransom is upon him."

key_terms.الْحَلاَلُ: the permissible one (one not in Ihram)
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in the state of Ihram (pilgrimal consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling for killing game in the Haram versus the Hill while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Reported by Shaykh al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the distinction between the sanctity of the location and the state of Ihram regarding game hunting. It establishes that while the prohibition on consumption applies strictly to game caught within the Haram boundaries, the financial ransom (fidya) remains the pilgrim's responsibility regardless of whether the catch occurred in the Haram or the open field (Hill).
